sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Gateshead froze most of its car park charges for 2026/27. The council's Cabinet report of 24 February 2026 proposed not raising charges at a large section of its car parks, because the 2022/23 and 2023/24 increases had affected usage; it noted that some car parks were under-used for reasons including work on the Tyne Bridge and the flyover, and proposed freezing prices to bring people back to the town centre [9]. On 26 February 2026 the council signed off most charges frozen, with modest rises: Queen Elizabeth Avenue short stay up by 10 to 20 pence to £2 and £3, higher seasonal permits at three sites, and second and third resident permits at £55 and £80 a year [10]. The proposed 2025/26 schedule left the Charles Street and Quarryfield Road tariffs unchanged from 2024/25, at £1.70 an hour and £5.10 for three hours at Charles Street and £2.60 for two hours and £5.70 for twelve at Quarryfield Road; it also lists unchanged tariffs at the two Heworth Metro-station car parks [11].

The Gateshead flyover has been closed and then removed. The council closed it on 13 December 2024 on safety grounds; Nexus withdrew the Metro between Central Station and Heworth on 19 December, and after temporary propping the service was restored on 31 December 2024 [13]. The last span was demolished on 29 September 2026, ending a six-month project that began in April; reported costs rose from £18 million, plus £2.5 million from the North East Combined Authority, to £31 million, which the chief executive said includes the emergency propping works [14]. The removal is described as opening the way for regeneration, including 1,100 homes [14]. In June 2026 the new Reform leadership of the council questioned the viability of the proposed Quayside arena [8].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main new supply is The Quays multi-storey. Gateshead Council appointed Willmott Dixon in April 2021 to build a £22.9 million, ten-storey car park of 1,000 spaces in the Baltic Quarter to support the planned arena and conference scheme [3]. A report of 5 October 2025 had it open with over 1,000 spaces, 45 large accessible spaces and 50 electric vehicle charging bays, at £2.60 for up to two hours and £5.70 for a full day, paid by app [0]. The arena scheme it was built to support has seen repeated delays: in March 2026 a contractor was expected to be appointed by the end of 2026, after a £24 million grant announced on 9 March, and the conference centre has been postponed [5].

The charging provision is not settled. The opening report gave 50 bays at 66p per kWh [0]. Zapmap, updated on 3 June 2026, lists 19 connectors on the APCOA network at 50p per kWh, so the number of chargers and their price are unconfirmed [2]. Elsewhere, the council said in June 2026 that it expects a planning application in September 2026, and a start on site in mid-2027, for the redevelopment of the Old Town Hall and surrounding surface car parks into 243 homes [15]. We found no sourced figures on Heworth capacities, on-street charges or event parking.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Gateshead data cover five car parks with 2,026 spaces, all from one regional live feed, and only ten days of readings each, so these are early figures. The Quays is listed with 987 spaces against 'over 1,000' in the report [0]; the Heworth capacities of 393 and 64 have no source we could open. Occupancy averaged about 8% on weekdays and 2% at weekends, weighted by spaces. Heworth Interchange long stay is the fullest at 21% on weekdays, followed by Charles Street (14.5%, of 27 spaces), Quarryfield Road (11%), Heworth short stay (1%) and The Quays (1%). Averaged by hour of the week, the busiest hour reaches 61% at Heworth long stay and 59% at Charles Street, but only 32% at Quarryfield Road and 5% at The Quays.

The Quays is the clearest case: with 987 spaces it is the largest car park in our data and the emptiest. Its reported charges of £2.60 for two hours and £5.70 for a day are close to Quarryfield Road's £2.60 for two hours and £5.70 for up to twelve in the proposed 2025/26 schedule [0][11]. Quarryfield Road is the second largest, with 555 spaces. Nearby venues price differently: the BALTIC car park charges £2 for up to an hour [22], and the Glasshouse car park is free for an hour and £5.95 all day, listing Quarryfield Road and The Quays as alternatives [23]. Metrocentre has almost 10,000 spaces, free during opening hours [21].
